newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Handlowy eyes three long-term investors.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Handlowy eyes three long-term investors.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy, which went on public offer on Monday, hopes to clinch deals with three financial institutions it picked for long-term investors before the end of subscription, the bank's president said.

Cezary Stypulkowski told a news conference Bank Handlowy, offering 45 percent of shares in retail and institutional tranches on subscription from May 26 to June 13 at 28-35 zlotys, has already selected three international institutions for a separate 42.9 percent tranche for long-term investors.
"From the bank's point of view the talks are over. Now we are waiting for the treasury ministry's decision and I expect it will come soon," he said.
"We have talked with several institutions I can say that this is now a group of three institutions," he added.
Asked whether the announcement could come before the end of the public subscription period Stypulkowski said: "I hope so."
He declined to confirm press reports that JP Morgan was among the selected institutions.

Stypulkowski said that while the sale price would be set in final talks with the selected institutions, the range set for the public offering would be a reference point and Handlowy would not be sold below the IPO range's minimum price.

The bank set aside 42.9 percent of Handlowy's shares which would represent 30 percent of the bank's capital after its convertible bonds issued on May 2 for the state treasury are converted into stock.

But because some shares could be moved to the retail tranche if demand proves strong Stypulkowski said the bank might consider allowing the long-term investors to get more shares by acquiring convertible bonds.
